newsitem.title: PERU: Japan backs Fujimori proposal in Lima crisis -Ikeda.
newsitem.headline: Japan backs Fujimori proposal in Lima crisis -Ikeda.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda said on Sunday the Japanese government fully backed President Alberto Fujimori's tough speech to Marxist rebels in which he urged them to lay down their arms and free all hostages.

"Although I cannot comment on the specifics, the proposal as a whole is the appropriate solution to a peaceful resolution to the crisis and the preservation of the lives of the hostages," he told Japanese reporters.

Ikeda was speaking after his second meeting with Fujimori since arriving on Thursday in Lima as Japan's on-the-spot advisor in the crisis, sparked on Tuesday when guerrillas of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) seized hundreds of hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence.
Japanese foreign ministry officials accompanying Ikeda would not comment on his plans for later on Sunday, but the minister was widely expected to be returning to Tokyo.

Ikeda said he had already been in contact with Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto in Tokyo about his discussions with Fujimori, and that Hashimoto was in complete agreement with the Peruvian leader's speech, which was broadcast to the nation late on Saturday.
Fujimori told the rebels a non-violent "way out" would be possible if they surrendered weapons and released their roughly 340 hostages.

"In my meeting with the president, he briefed me on the contents of his message to the rebels, which we fully support," Ikeda said. "My impression of President Fujimori is of a man fighting hard to reach the best solution to a tough situation, all the while taking into account the preservation of lives."
Ikeda said that Fujimori seemed weathered but more confident in his second meeting compared to the first.
"Although there is no change in his resolve to break the stalemate, I felt that in the earlier meeting, he seemed undecided about what exactly to do.
"But tonight, although he looked weary from concentration, I felt a sense of confidence from him that a way out will definitely open up," he added.
